vocab.definition: a biological catalyst that speeds up reactions.
the molecule an enzyme acts on.
the part of the enzyme the substrate fits into.
the active site changes shape and stops working.

misconceptions.wrong: Enzymes are killed by high temperature.
misconceptions.right: Enzymes are not alive — they are denatured.

misconceptions.wrong: One enzyme works on any substrate.
misconceptions.right: Enzymes are specific to one substrate shape.

misconceptions.wrong: Denaturing can be reversed by cooling.
misconceptions.right: Denaturing is permanent — the shape is lost.

infoPanels.title: LOCK-AND-KEY MODEL
infoPanels.secondaryContent: Only a substrate with the right shape fits the active site.

questions.text: Describe what is meant by an enzyme. [2 marks]
Explain why each enzyme only works on one type of substrate. [2 marks]
Explain what happens to an enzyme above its optimum temperature. [3 marks]
Complete the table of enzymes using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: ______ breaks starch into ______ ; protease breaks protein into amino acids.

questions.text: An enzyme works best at pH 7. Predict what happens to its rate at pH 3. [2 marks]
Explain how bile increases the rate of fat digestion. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Substrate must fit the active site — like a key in a lock.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does the rate fall on BOTH sides of the optimum temperature?
